summary: Marcel Hofinger worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte.

Marcel Mauss worked in religious studies, philosophy, and other fields, studying in Bordeaux, Utrecht, Leiden, Oxford, and at EPHE under Durkheim, Lévi, and others. He held chairs at the EPHE (from 1901) and the Collège de France (1931–1940).

Marcelle Lalou specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, completing her doctorate at the EPHE and studying under Przyluski, Lévi, Bacot, and Pelliot. She taught at the EPHE (1938–1963) and edited the Journal Asiatique (1950–1966).
Marco Ferrante works in Indology and philosophy. He has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and Sapienza University of Rome (attested 2014).
Marco Walther is a scholar in Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcus Bingenheimer works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and computational fields. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and Nagoya, and held posts at the Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (2005–2011) and Temple University (2012–2015).
Marek Mejor works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held a fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982) and a professorship at the University of Warsaw (attested 2000–2010).
Marek Zemánek specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Dongguk University, Seoul National University, and Charles University, completing his dissertation under Radek Chlup.
Marek Zvelebil was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Sheffield and subsequently held a post there from circa 1981 to 2011.
Margaret Cone works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the University of Cambridge and Darwin College, Cambridge (attested 1996).
Margaret Gouin specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

Margaret H. Dornish worked in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at USC, Yale, and Claremont Graduate University, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).

Margaret Mead was an anthropologist who studied at Barnard and Columbia under Franz Boas. Her career included long-term positions at the American Museum of Natural History (1926, 1946–1969) and Columbia University (1954–1978).

Margaret R. Miles is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. After earning her PhD at the Graduate Theological Union, she taught at Harvard Divinity School (circa 1978–1996) and served as dean of the Graduate Theological Union (1996–2001).

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer specializes in religious studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower and was mentored postdoctorally by Xiuping Hong.

Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at St. Petersburg University, she had a long career at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts, curating Central Asian manuscripts (1982–2005).
Margarita Kleibel works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Klaus-Dieter Mathes for her master's degree and under Karin Preisendanz.

Maria Heim works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her BA at Reed College and her PhD at Harvard University under Charles Hallisey, later serving as Associate Professor at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

Marian Ury was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and served as a professor of East Asian languages and comparative literature at UC Davis from 1969 to 1995.

Marianne Pieper studied at HWP and completed her habilitation at Magdeburg. She held visiting professorships at Hamburg and Kassel, and served as professor of sociology at the University of Hamburg from 1996 to 2015.
